document.title: 2023 NBA Collective Bargaining Agreement
document.scope: trade machine rules and apron restrictions

aggregated_standard.incoming_formula: 100% of aggregated pre-trade salaries + applicable allowance
aggregated_standard.reference: Article VII, Section 6(j)(1)(ii); Section 2(e)(4) row H

expanded.incoming_formula: max(min(200% outgoing + applicable allowance, outgoing + scaled $7.5m), 125% outgoing + applicable allowance)
expanded.reference: Article VII, Section 6(j)(1)(iv); Section 2(e)(4) row E

allowance_reduction.post_trade_first_apron_rule: If post-assignment Apron Team Salary would exceed the First Apron, the $250,000 allowance in Sections 6(j)(1)(i)-(v) is reduced to $0.

hard_cap_behavior.current_year: A team may not execute a listed transaction if immediately afterward its Apron Team Salary exceeds the applicable apron, and after executing it may not exceed that apron for the rest of the Salary Cap Year.
hard_cap_behavior.late_year_future_year: For rows E-J after the regular season through June 30, the CBA also tests and hard-caps the subsequent Salary Cap Year under the assumptions in Section 2(e)(3).

cash.reference: Article VII, Section 8(a); Section 2(e)(4) row I

notes: Apron Team Salary is not identical to ordinary Team Salary.
It adds excluded performance bonuses and specified young-player salary amounts, applies RFA/qualifying-offer treatment, and removes specified free-agent, exception and incomplete-roster amounts.
The trade machine therefore accepts an authoritative Apron Team Salary when available and labels contract-sum estimates as estimates.

engine_guardrails.matching_salary_overrides: Each player asset can provide an outgoing_salary_for_matching and incoming_salary_for_matching override for special CBA cases such as trade bonuses or other salary-treatment rules.
engine_guardrails.trade_eligibility: Each asset carries trade_eligible and consent flags. The engine fails closed when a selected player is ineligible or required consent is absent.
engine_guardrails.unknown_rules: If inputs required for a special CBA rule are not known, the result is qualified instead of silently assuming legality.
